label: Chapter 1: The giant and the hand

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Start me with the big one. Literally.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Okay. This is a legend, not history.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Long ago, a giant called Druon Antigoon lived by the river Scheldt.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Of course he did.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He guarded a crossing and charged a toll.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Anyone who couldn't pay lost a hand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He cut it off and threw it into the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's a very specific business model.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then a young Roman soldier called Silvius Brabo arrives.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He beats the giant, cuts off the giant's own hand, and throws it into the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Poetic justice. With a knife.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the story says that's how the city got its name.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Dutch name is Antwerpen. The tale reads it as "hand werpen," which means hand throwing.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh, that's good. So the whole city is named after a thrown hand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not quite. That's the folk explanation.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The sources I checked say some specialists dispute it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Another idea connects the name to a word for a jetty or landing place by the water.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A jetty. Much less fun.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Much less fun.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So where do I see the hand?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The main square, the Grote Markt, in front of the town hall.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There's a fountain by the sculptor Jef Lambeaux, put up in 1887.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Brabo stands on top, about to throw.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: At the bottom, the hand is already in the air.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And I'm not allowed to pretend it's real.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You can pretend. Just remember it's a legend.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Noted. Bet number one. Somebody tonight mentions another hand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll get there. Next, a tall one.
